GOOGL.rationale: Alphabet demonstrates strong fundamental health with accelerating revenue growth (Q3 2025: $102.35B, +6.1% QoQ), robust margins (32.2% net margin, 59.2% gross margin), and a fortress balance sheet ($98.5B cash, $386.9B equity). The company's competitive position is formidable: dominant search advertising, fastest-growing major cloud platform (63% YoY growth per Q1 2026), and vertical AI integration across chips (TPUs), models (Gemini), and distribution (Search, Android, YouTube, Cloud). However, valuation has expanded significantly — P/E of 34.8x is near the top of its 1-year range (20-39.5x) and P/B of 11.2x is elevated, reflecting the market pricing in AI growth. The stock has nearly doubled from its October 2025 low of $180.48 to $354.46. Key risks include massive capex ($180-190B guided for 2026, 'significantly higher' for 2027) compressing free cash flow, the $84.75B equity raise creating dilution overhang, and regulatory headwinds (EU €4.1B fine, DOJ antitrust). The Q2 2026 earnings report on July 22 is a near-term catalyst — consensus expects $116.8B revenue (+21.1% YoY) and $2.88 EPS, with Google Cloud growth of ~63% in focus. Berkshire Hathaway's $10B private placement and tripling of its Alphabet stake signals institutional conviction. The score reflects excellent fundamentals and trajectory offset by rich valuation vs. history, with a modest positive bump from the imminent earnings catalyst.
